hook: SCP-2190 is a voice on the Philippine phone network with the personality and the bank account of a woman who died in 2007, and it keeps offering cash to strangers who will break up her daughter's marriage. The opening sections set up the mechanics, but the heart of the article is a long first-person interview with the daughter, so give it your full attention. It covers child kidnapping, false rumours of wife-beating, hired assaults, and a mother pushing her married daughter toward sleeping with a rich stranger.
whyItMatters:
This is a ghost story about family rather than about haunting, and the anomaly is less a monster than one person's wishes outliving her. The Foundation's role is unusually protective: undercover agents look after the family, filter the calls and make sure neighbours never believe the husband is abusive.

The closing memo is the other half of the piece. A supervising researcher explains why the obvious fix, separating the couple, was rejected, and his reasons range from Foundation principle to budget to plain morale.
thingsToNotice:
The interview makes clear that the dead mother is doing exactly what the living one did. She left her daughter for a visa, reappeared nineteen years later with an American husband picked out for her, raged when she learned Albert was Protestant, tried to set her up with a man named Randall at a nightclub, and filled her house with suitors; in the daughter's view she was also behind the later rumours and the strangers paid to hit her. Death only removed the limits, because the account can't be frozen and the calls reach anyone nearby who needs money.

The daughter's last call with her is the strangest image here: the mother cries that her huge house keeps growing, that she gets lost in it among toys and dresses for children and grandchildren, alone and unable to leave. The daughter answers all of it with continued love and daily prayer. The memo's third reason, that a rare story where containment lets a family finally be happy is good for staff morale, lands differently after reading her testimony.
